questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 1. Determine the frequency, wavelength, and momentum of a photon if the energy of the photon is equal to the rest energy of an electron.

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 2. A fan rotates 1500 times per minute. After turning off the switch, it stops after 4 minutes. What is the angular deceleration of the fan? Determine how many times the fan will rotate before it comes to a complete stop.

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 3. $6000 \mathrm{MJ}$ of kinetic energy is transferred to an artificial satellite of $200 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass while it is taken to a particular altitude from the earth's surface. At what altitude will the satellite revolve around the earth? The mass of earth is $6 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$, radius is $6400 \mathrm{~km}$ and $\mathrm{G}=6.6 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{Nm}^{2} \mathrm{~kg}^{-2}$.

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 4. A charge of $20 \mu \mathrm{C}$ makes an electric field. There are two points at distance $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the charge. What is the work done to take an electron from one point to the other?

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 5. A pond filled with water has a depth of 10 m, length of 10 m, and width of 5 m. To empty the pond in 30 minutes, what horsepower pump should be used? (Given $g = 980 \, \text{cm/s}^2$)

questions.question: 8. A diffraction grating has 6000 lines per centimeter, through which the second-order spectrum of sodium light is obtained. If the wavelengths of two sodium lights are 5890Å and 5896Å, what is the angular separation between them?

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 9. A 30-year-old woman leaves her 10-year-old daughter behind and goes on a space journey in a spaceship traveling at 0.98c. She spends 30 years in space according to Earth time and then returns. How old will they be after she returns?

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 12. An object is dropped from a certain height. At a height of 10 meters above the ground, the kinetic energy is twice the potential energy. From what height was the object dropped?

questions.subject: Physics(15)
questions.question: 13. Provide the mathematical definition of the intensity of a wave. If the intensity of a sound is increased by a factor of 3, by how many decibels will the sound intensity level change?

$i = 30 \sin{\left ( 107 t + \frac{\pi}{2} \right )}$

2. The root mean square (RMS) value,
3. The value of the current at $t = 0$.

questions.question: 9. If the lines $3x + by + 1 = 0$ and $ax + 6y + 1 = 0$ intersect at the point $(5, 4)$, determine the values of $a$ and $b$. If the first line intersects the x-axis at point $A$ and the second line intersects the y-axis at point $B$, find the equation of the line passing through points $A$ and $B$.

questions.subject: Math(15)
questions.question: 10. The points $A(5,3), B(-2,0)$ and $C(1,1)$ are on a circle. Find the distance between the center of the circle and center of gravity of the triangle $A B C$.

questions.subject: Math(15)
questions.question: 12. Mr. Rahman wants to buy at least one kilogram each of apples and grapes, with a maximum budget of 130 Taka. When he visits the shop, he finds that within his budget, he can buy either a maximum of three kilograms of grapes and four kilograms of apples, or two kilograms of grapes and seven kilograms of apples. What is the maximum total weight of fruit he can buy within his budget?

questions.subject: Math(15)
questions.question: 13. In a college of 40 students in the 12th grade, 20 students play football, 25 students play cricket, and 10 students play both football and cricket. One student is randomly selected. What is the probability that the student plays cricket given that they play football?

questions.question: 15. Given $n$ distinct objects, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r+1$, $r+2$, and $r+3$ at a time are in the ratio 15:24:28. Find the values of $n$ and $r$.

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 6. The polymer compound $(\text{C}_2\text{F}_4)_n$ was prepared in the presence of a sulfur-containing catalyst. It contains 0.012% sulfur. If there are 3 sulfur atoms per polymer molecule, find the value of $n$.

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 7. Glucose is a thermolabile substance. At 100°C, its solubility in water is 45.5 g/L. The relative density of water at this temperature is 0.95. When a 250 mL saturated solution of glucose is cooled to 100°C, 11.5 g of glucose crystallizes out. What is the solubility of glucose at 100°C?

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 8. At 250°C and infinite dilution, the equivalent conductivity of a monobasic weak acid is $388.5 \, \Omega^{-1} \text{cm}^2 \text{equiv}^{-1}$. If the degree of ionization is 6%, calculate the relative conductivity of a 0.1 M solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 10. At 25°C, the partition constant of H₂S between water and benzene is given as $\frac{[H_{2}S]_{H_{2}O}}{[H_{2}S]_{C_{6}H_{6}}} = 0.167$. To extract 90% of H₂S in a single step from a 0.1 M H₂S aqueous solution of 1.0 liter volume, what is the minimum volume of benzene required?

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)

11. At $327^\circ \text{C}$, the decomposition rate of HI is given by:
$- \frac{d C_{HI}}{dt} = k C_{HI}^{2}$
where $k = 4 \times 10^{-6} \text{ L mol}^{-1} \text{ sec}^{-1}$. How many molecules decompose per second per cubic centimeter at atmospheric pressure?

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 12. 5 grams of copper(II) sulfate is dissolved in water to make a 200 cm³ solution. A 20 cm³ aliquot of this solution is taken in a conical flask, and after adding a slight excess of KI, it is titrated with Na₂S₂O₃ solution. After titration, 19.5 cm³ of 0.05 M Na₂S₂O₃ solution was required. Calculate the percentage of copper(II) sulfate in the solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry(15)
questions.question: 13. An organic compound A with the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₂, when reduced by LiAlH₄, yields two different compounds B and C. When compound B is oxidized, it produces compound D. Upon reacting compound D with an aqueous solution of NaOH and heating, compound E is obtained. When compound E is subjected to hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst, compound C is obtained. Compound D, when further oxidized, yields a monobasic acid F with a molecular weight of 60. Determine the structures of A, B, C, D, E, and F.
